To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method for the synthesis of complex molecular scaffolds via a dehydrogenation reaction.
we have developed an efficient method to synthesize highly substituted, polycyclic molecules from simple olefins and dienes via a novel Pd(II)-catalyzed deoxygenative Diels-Alder reaction.
we have developed a Pd(0)-catalyzed dehydrosilylation of terminal olefins, which has been extended to a dehydrogenation reaction with a bis-sulfoxide ligand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new catalytic methods for the construction of complex organic molecules.
the design, development and application of new methods for organic synthesis.
developing novel methods for the synthesis of biologically active natural products and related molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dehydrogenative cycloaddition reaction described herein is an efficient and selective method for the construction of complex cyclohexenes from simple starting materials.
this reaction is a new method to access highly substituted cycloadduct molecules.

we report the first example of a dehydrogenation Diels-Alder cycloaddition that is mediated by a transition metal catalyst and proceeds under mild reaction conditions to afford highly substituted, complex cycloaddition products in good yields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Pd(IV) intermediate undergoes a C-H activation and an intramolecular cyclization to generate the cycloadduct.
we have discovered a new type of Diels-Alder cycloaddition that is catalytic, stereospecific, and that proceeds with high levels of regio- and diastereoselectivity.
we have developed a method for the construction of a complex molecular skeleton from simple starting materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a C-H bond can be used as a handle to access a new molecular scaffold.
a C-H oxidation reaction can be used to build a molecular skeleton, rather than simply modify a pre-existing one.
C-H activation chemistry can be used to build molecular complexity.
